{{Quote|General, prepare your troops for a surface attack.''"''<br />''"''Yes, my lord.|Darth Vader and Veers preparing for the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]|audio=PrepareYourTroopsForASurfaceAttack.flac|<ref name="ESB" />}}
'''Maximilian Veers''' was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Major General]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]], famous for his leadership at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|assault]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] and other battles. He also was the father of [[Zevulon Veers]]. He [[Death/Legends|died]] in the [[Battle of Balmorra]] in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]].

==Biography==
===Early life and career===
[[File:Veers_SWGTCG.jpg|left|thumb|Colonel Veers early in his military career.]]
Maximilian Veers was the son of a middle-class working [[Veers family|family]]<ref name="NEGTC" /> on the [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|ecumenopolis]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Denon/Legends|Denon]] in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]].<ref name="SWCE" /> He joined the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] and, while there, decided to train towards a career in the [[Assault Armor Division/Legends|Assault Armor Division]], where he might operate the mechanical behemoths that were the [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transports]].<ref name="GG3" /> He believed the massive vehicles introduced during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="SWR55">[[Republic 55|''Republic'' 55]]</ref> best embodied his own personality as well as that of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. He took up his training with rigorous determination, showing a surprising intellect and initiative after emerging from several "suicide missions" by surpassing his mission assignments. Veers' superiors finding him both skillful and dangerous, was promoted to the rank of [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] upon graduation and an assignment as commander of an [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-AT]]. As a test of his abilities, he was soon shipped to a barbaric and backwater [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] world called [[Culroon III/Legends|Culroon III]].<ref name="GG3" />

The Culroon III campaign was designed to either make or break Veers. If he failed, he was likely to perish.<ref name="GG3" /> He quickly learned that the Empire did not tolerate incompetence and failure. During the attempt to pacify the natives of Culroon III, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Irrv]] had ordered for Lieutenant Veers to remain confined to the base while he and an Imperial party went to negotiate a peace with the Culroon natives. Veers had warned that it was a trap and that Irrv should bring armored support to deter any would-be ambushers. General Irrv did not listen and paid the price with his life when he was executed for incompetence after the Culroon natives deceived and [[Insurrection on Culroon III|killed]] most of his party. If it had not been for Lieutenant Veers's quick thinking and disregard of a direct order, the Imperial party would have been utterly slaughtered.<ref name="promos">{{WEGCite|story=The Promotion of Lieutenant Veers|book=The Star Wars Sourcebook|reprint=1}}</ref> For his bravery and brilliance in saving the Culroon mission's [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] detail, Veers was promoted to [[Major/Legends|major]].<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:Maximilian_Veers.jpg|thumb|Maximilian Veers]]
Major Veers [[Marriage/Legends|married]] and had a son named [[Zevulon Veers|Zevulon]]. When Zevulon was only a young boy, Veers lost his [[Maximilian Veers's wife|wife]] to a rare disease during a family vacation.<ref name="DESB" /> Devastated by the death of his wife, Veers buried his grief in his military career. This began to affect his relationship with his son, who he advised to honor his mother by joining the [[Sub-Adult Group/Legends|Sub-Adult Group]], a youth paramilitary organization of the Empire.<ref name="NEGTC" />

Veers's devotion to the army seemed to pay off, as he was granted the rank of colonel and the command of an Imperial garrison on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. Veers was also widely recognized as an authority on the AT-AT, and often returned to [[Carida/Legends|Carida]] to guest-lecture at AT-AT training courses and demonstrate prototypes of new AT-AT models. During one of these demonstrations, shortly before [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], Veers came to the attention of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] when he defeated a [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Skirmish on Carida|invasion force]].<ref name="EAW">''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''</ref>

At this point, however, Veers's career seemed to stagnate. Veers lacked the aristocratic connections needed to move up in rank,<ref name="NEGTC" /> and questions had arisen regarding his methods of career advancement.<ref name="GG3" /> Worse, during one of the training courses on Carida, a promising [[Cadet/Legends|Cadet]] named [[Davin Felth/Legends|Davin Felth]] lowered his walker to its knees in order to prevent the opposing force from exploiting the weakness its long legs presented. The weakness threatened Veers's career, as it was so closely tied to the success of the walkers. Veers buried the incident by reassigning Felth to the infantry.<ref name="Desert Wind">{{StoryCite|story=When the Desert Wind Turns: The Stormtrooper's Tale|book=Tales from the Mos Eisley Cantina}}</ref>

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|Colonel, you are too important to the Empire to languish in a prison camp.|Darth Vader, freeing Veers on Zaloriis|<ref name="SW:GB" />}}
[[File:GeneralVeers_Murray_TCG.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[General/Legends|General]] Veers in his [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-AT]] pilot armor during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]].]]
Veers had been selected for a position on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], as a ground commander, and as an academic instructor. With Felth out of the way, this seemed the perfect opportunity to achieve an elite position. The assignment turned out to be another dead end, as Veers had only just arrived in-system at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. A Rebel [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] fighter spotted his shuttle and forced a crash landing on the jungle moon of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. For some time, Colonel Veers survived on emergency rations and local wildlife before he contacted an assault force led by Major [[Brenn Tantor]], which was able to rescue him.<ref name="SW:FC">''[[Star Wars: Force Commander]]''</ref>

Having had his new position blown out from under him, Colonel Veers returned to his garrison on [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]. There he helped [[Corellian Security Force|CorSec]] Inspectors [[Hal Horn|Hal]] and [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] put an end to the criminal [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] lieutenant, [[Zekka Thyne]], by [[Capture of Zekka Thyne|storming]] his fortress on the notion that Thyne was harboring [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] insurgents. Impressed by Veers's performance in removing Black Sun's presence near [[Coronet City/Legends|Coronet City]], [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] recommended the brilliant ground commander to Darth Vader.<ref name="ST">"[[Side Trip]]"</ref>

As it turned out, the destruction of the Death Star aided Veers's career in the long run. The deaths of so many high-ranking officers aboard the station had left a power vacuum that Veers stepped into following the raid on Thyne's stronghold.<ref name="GG3" />

Veers was able to continue work in secret on the new AT-AT prototype on [[Zaloriis/Legends|Zaloriis]], which he described as "''the'' walker". Unexpectedly, the Zalorians declared independence from the Empire and abducted him. He was later [[Zaloriis campaign/Legends|rescued]] by Darth Vader. Together, Vader and Veers completed work on the prototype and used it to crush the Zalorian rebellion, destroying [[Zaloriis City]] in the process.<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

After his defiance of direct orders led to the success of an [[Insurrection on Culroon III|imperial operation]] on [[Culroon III/Legends|Culroon III]], Veers was promoted to [[Major General]] over the heads of several [[High Colonel/Legends|High Colonel]]s, placing him in command of [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron's]] ground troops. Despite the questions that had surfaced concerning his career advancement, not a single high colonel questioned Veers' unorthodox promotion to Vader's fleet, and these issues quickly faded. Veers recruited only the best pilots to serve in his [[Thundering Herd/Legends|Thundering Herd]] AT-AT squadron.<ref name="GG3" /> In [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]], he personally recruited several pilots from the [[Raithal Academy/Legends|Raithal Academy]].<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2015 Topps Star Wars Illustrated: The Empire Strikes Back|cardname=One Year Earlier: General Veers}}</ref> Often, he would pilot an extra armored and more powerful walker.<ref name="EAW" />

His new appointment was the pinnacle of success for someone in Veers's position, and he wasted no time proving himself. Just weeks after the promotion, Veers had his forces pared down by ten percent, yet efficiency had risen by 50 percent. His timing was impeccable, for in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] an [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd]] [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]] from Death Squadron had discovered the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command's]] secret [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the planet [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="GG3" />

[[File:Veers-hd.png|thumb|200px|Veers speaks to Darth Vader.]]

Veers's most notable success occurred at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] when he was given the chance to correct a mistake caused by the incompetent [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Ozzel]]. General Veers lived up to both his reputation and [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader's expectations by quickly deploying his armored regiment, designated [[Blizzard Force/Legends|Blizzard Force]], into the [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] mountain valley and personally destroying the [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|shield generator]] protecting the Rebel base.<ref name="ESB" /> Shortly after the destruction of the shield generator, Rebel [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeder]] [[Rebel pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek "Hobbie" Klivian]] flew his damaged vessel directly into the cockpit of Veers's [[Blizzard 1/Legends|''Blizzard'' 1]] AT-AT.<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref>

Both men miraculously survived the incident but came out badly injured. General Veers attempted to flee the bridge of his AT-AT, but was not swift enough and a falling support beam crushed his leg bones into pieces so small that reconstruction and [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] could not restore them. Veers, like many in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], held a dislike for cybernetics and refused to have his legs replaced with [[Cybernetics/Legends|prosthetics]]. Because of this, Veers would be confined to a [[Repulsorlift chair/Legends|hoverchair]] for the rest of his life.<ref name="NEGTC" />

===After Hoth===
Although the Battle of Hoth was a great victory for him, bringing him fame and glory, it was overshadowed by a report from his son's [[Commission for the Preservation of the New Order/Legends|COMPNOR]] [[Sub-Adult Group/Legends|SAGroup]] commander. The commander reported that Zevulon Veers had gone missing during a SAGroup mission dealing with Rebel spies. However, the honored General suspected that his son had defected to the Rebellion and disowned him. The betrayal of his son brought shame and dishonor to the Veers name despite the General's victory at [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. He would suffer from the ignominy his son brought forth for the rest of his life.<ref name="NEGTC" />

[[4 ABY/Legends|Nearly a year later]], General Veers was on a planetside mission when the ''Executor'' was destroyed over [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="NEGTC" />

After the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], General Veers served under command of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Sander Delvardus]]. Delvardus soon became one of the first Imperial [[Warlord/Legends|Warlords]] and created the Imperial splinter faction known as the [[Eriadu Authority]]. This was criticized by General Veers and other Imperial [[Officer/Legends|officers]] serving under him.<ref name="TIW:DoaE2" />

In the following years, he searched for a new Imperial warlord to serve. Many times he was shunned away or rejected downright because of his relationship with Lord Vader. Many post-Endor officers despised anyone who had served and survived Darth Vader and wanted nothing to do with them. Nonetheless, it was believed that Veers served as a [[Clone template/Legends|genetic template]] for Grand Admiral Thrawn's [[Mount Tantiss project|clone]] [[Thrawn's army|army]].<ref name="NEGTC" />

[[File:Veers_last_battle.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Veers leads the infantry assault on Balmorra's capital [[Bin Prime]] from a repulsor transport.]]

For [[Operation Shadow Hand]], [[Executor (Imperial rank)|Executor]] [[Sedriss QL]], who hated Veers, demoted him to the rank of captain but nonetheless put him in charge of the Imperial ground forces in the [[Battle of Balmorra]]. Maximilian Veers, one of the Empire's greatest ground tacticians and heroes, perished on that fateful mission.<ref name="NEGTC" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|They call ''that'' a defense?|Veers during battle|<ref name="EAW" />}}
Veers was a ruthless and aggressive officer who enjoyed wreaking havoc with the destructive Imperial ground forces,<ref name="EAWGG">[[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Empire at War'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> but was also an honorable frontline commander who was not opposed to putting himself in harm's way. These traits earned him the respect of both Darth Vader and Grand Admiral Thrawn for his courage under fire.<ref name="ST" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MaximilianVeers-NEGTC.png|thumb|150px|General Veers]]
Maximilian Veers was portrayed by [[Julian Glover]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. [[George Lucas]] would later cast Glover as the villainous Walter Donovan in ''Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'', reuniting him with [[Harrison Ford]] (although ''Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade'' was the first film in which Glover and Ford appeared together onscreen, having shared no scenes in ''The Empire Strikes Back''). Veers was voiced by [[Gordon Gould]] in the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|audio drama version]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back''. [[Guy Siner]] provided the voice of Veers in [[Star Wars: Force Commander|''Force Commander'']]. His voice in the [[2005]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'' was provided by [[Jamie Glover]], Julian's son.

In the novel adaptation of the screenplay of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', General Veers was killed shortly after the destruction of the shield generator during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. The snowspeeder pilot [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek Klivian]] suffered severe damage to his craft and sped it into a suicide attack on Veers's walker. The resulting explosion destroyed the "head" of the walker, killing Veers and his crew. This scene was actually filmed for ''The Empire Strikes Back'' but was ultimately cut.

''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] released in [[2001]], portrays Veers as a colonel at the beginning of the [[Zaloriis campaign/Legends|Battle of Zaloriis]] and being promoted to general afterward. "Congratulations, ''General'' Veers," Vader tells him. This may be inconsistent with other sources. However, a stormtrooper calls him "General" before this promotion, when Veers arrives to take the prototype AT-AT. Also, when the player selects Veers, he sometimes responds by saying "General Veers, my Lord?" The game's [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]] incorrectly states he led the [[Imperial Marines/Legends|Imperial Marines]] at the Battle of Hoth.

In the [[2006]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Tarkin]] states that Veers designed the AT-AT personally. In the game he commands a modified AT-AT.

{{Noncanonstart|legends=1}}
Veers also appeared in a skit for the [[Canon|non-canon]] special ''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars Episode II]]'', where he tells the AT-ATs to start their attack on Echo Base, only to be completely dumbfounded when two of the AT-ATs jumped out of line to participate in a race that greatly resembled a freeway race by teenagers, resulting in one of the AT-ATs being totaled. When Vader asks for the results of the mission, Veers was in such a state of shock that he wasn't able to give any, causing him to instead cover Vader's hologram with a plastic coffee cup.

General Veers briefly appeared in the [[2006]] video game [[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy|Lego Star Wars 2: The Original Trilogy]] and the [[2007]] video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' at the beginning of the "Escape from Echo Base" and "Hoth Battle" levels (''The Empire Strikes Back'').
{{Noncanonend}}
